rows.threat: Escape and exfiltration from a migration run
rows.here: The egress proxy tunnels only to allowlisted registry host names on allowed ports, resolves each name once and refuses one that resolves to a private, loopback or link-local address, refuses addresses written as hosts (including short and hexadecimal IPv4 forms) and plain HTTP; under docker, an analysis container runs as a non-root user with no capabilities, no new privileges, no network interface but loopback and no DNS, a read-only root and read-only inputs, and is killed for memory, CPU time and wall clock, each reported as such; a fetch container reaches the npm registry through the proxy, is refused elsewhere, cannot connect directly or resolve names, and is never shown the repository; the Kubernetes Jobs and NetworkPolicies are held to the schema by kubeconform and deny an analysis all traffic and a fetch all but the proxy; the Fly machines are one-shot, never restarted and destroyed at the wall clock; and invariant migrate believes a sandbox's result only as files inside the repository and never writes through a link.

refuses a host that is not on the allowlist, without resolving or reaching it
refuses an address written as the host, and a port that is not HTTPS's
refuses an allowed name that resolves to a private or link-local address

rows.threat: A wrong, compromised or impersonated bundle service
rows.here: A consumer reading published bundles opens each only with a key its provider serves from its own domain at /.well-known/invariant.json, over HTTPS, following redirects only on that host and reading at most 64 KiB; a signature is verified against the listed public key, whose id is recomputed from the key, so a bundle labelled with a listed key id but signed by another is refused, as is one signed by a key the document does not list, one signed before its key was added or after it stopped signing, anything a revoked key signed, and a bundle for another API than asked.
rows.elsewhere: When a bundle was published is the time the distributing service records, since a bundle carries none; a service that backdated it could only matter for a key past not_after that also leaked, which its provider revokes. Recording publication times and serving the endpoint from a CDN are the service's, in its repository.

titles: opens one the current key signed
opens one a retired key signed while it still signed, and refuses one it signed after
refuses one published before its key was added
refuses everything a revoked key signed, whenever it was signed
refuses one signed by a key the provider does not list, however valid its signature
refuses an API the document does not list, or a bundle for another API than asked
is refused when a key's id is not its key's, a time has no zone, or a key is listed twice
is read from its own domain over https
follows a redirect on its own host, and no other
is read no further than 64 KiB, whether or not it says how long it is

outOfScope: Cross-tenant probes on every endpoint of the control plane, in the service's repository.
Token scope escapes against the control plane's API, in the service's repository.
Sandbox escape attempts against the hosted playground, in the service's repository.
SSRF through the service's /v1/propose endpoint and playground as endpoints; the document reader they share is covered here.
found: The proxy piped a caller's connection to the upstream as soon as it forwarded an Upgrade handshake, so a second request on the same socket reached the upstream outside the base path and unexamined; an h2c upgrade was passed on the same way.
The proxy forwarded /api/..%2fadmin, which a server that decodes before routing reads as /admin, and answered a Host no URL can hold with 500.
A captured webhook delivery sent again under a fresh delivery id, or under another event's name, was handled a second time.
A $ref to a file committed as a link was followed outside the repository, reading the file it pointed at into the document.
A $ref to #/components/schemas/__proto__ or .../constructor resolved to a JavaScript prototype and counted as defined; a schema gathered from a file named __proto__ was lost.
A Change naming prototype compiled without an issue into a program the runtime refuses at load.
A field name holding a sentence was written into Jev's question as an option; a choice that was not a key threw; a field named __proto__ vanished from both judges' scores.
A schema at 2^depth places made the compiler write a program that doubled with each level, and sixteen levels overflowed its stack.
The runtime's time budget, in TypeScript and in Go, was never read for a program shorter than 256 instructions.

A migration wrote a symbol map's helpers path and a regenerated file's path wherever ../ or an absolute path pointed, wrote through a package.json or source file committed as a link, and migrated a sibling checkout whose path its own was a prefix of.
Every third-party GitHub Action was referenced by a tag its owner can move.
